title: Mexican Grandma Tries Vegan Pozole — Tasting, Garnishes, and Substitutions
summary: BuzzFeed Nifty’s short feature follows Yolanda (the grandmother) and Desiree as they discuss and taste a vegan pozole. The segment frames posole as traditional Mexican-American comfort food, detailing typical ingredients, garnishes, and serving styles, then probes how a plant-based version compares in flavor and texture. The conversation touches on pork or chicken bases, garnishes (cabbage, onions, radishes, lime, tostadas), and spice choices (sauces like Tabasco), while also noting that vegan substitutions (tofu or tempeh) can be indistinguishable to conventional palates. Viewers observe tasting notes about broth thickness, meat-replacement texture, and overall acceptance, with recommendations for serving and possible adjustments (more meat or fixings on the side) for different preferences.

sections.title: Family context and posole as comfort food

sections.title: Posole ingredients and garnishes
sections.description: The speakers describe common building blocks for posole and its garnishes, noting that lime quantities differ among households and that garnishes are integral to the dish, not mere toppings.

sections.title: Tasting notes: broth, texture, and flavor
sections.description: A tasting moment highlights a thick, not fully clear broth and compares the texture to traditional red pozole, noting the bite and mouthfeel of the meat substitutes.

sections.title: Spice preferences and condiments
sections.description: Discussion of spiciness, preferred sauces, and how lime is variably used, reflecting personal and cultural taste differences.

sections.description: Conversations acknowledge that the vegan pozole can pass as non-vegan to some tasters, with references to common plant-based proteins that could stand in for meat.

considerations for adding more meat in traditional variants
